articles.title: US Open: No. 3 Jessica Pegula survives rough start vs. Emma Navarro to set up clash with No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka
articles.summary: Pegula and Sabalenka are both in contention for the WTA No. 1 ranking.
articles.body:
Jessica Pegula didn't exactly play like the No. 3 player in the world on Tuesday, but she's still alive at the US Open.

The top-seeded American in the field overcame an awful start in the quarterfinals to defeat No. 26 seed and countrywoman Emma Navarro 3-6, 6-4, 6-3. Her reward will be a matchup with No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka on Thursday, in the latter's third straight US Open semifinal.

Pegula will have to overcome history to go further. Sabalenka ended both of those runs, with a straight-sets win in the 2024 final and a three-set thriller in last year's semifinal. Sabalenka leads their career head-to-head 9-4, though Pegula won their most recent meeting 6-4, 6-7, 6-0 in Berlin earlier this year.

Both Sabalenka and Pegula remain in contention for the WTA's No. 1 ranking coming out of the tournament, though all of that goes up in smoke if No. 2 Elena Rybakina wins her quarterfinal match against Qinwen Zheng on Wednesday.

If Rybakina does lose, she still becomes No. 1 unless Pegula, Sabalenka or Coco Gauff win the title. Like Pegula, Sabalenka took a major step toward that goal on Tuesday with an intense three-set win over No. 6 seed Linda Noskova .

Jessica Pegula clearly frustrated in first set

Pegula had to do plenty of work just to keep her hopes alive. Facing a fellow daughter of a billionaire family — the jokes are too easy to bother with — she was inexplicably tight in the first set.

Her serve was particularly rough early on. She rarely got her first serve in, landing only 11 of 28 in her first three service games. Her second serve was easy to abuse when it actually landed, winning only 6-of-17 points on it while committing five double faults in those same three games. Navarro, who entered the match with an 0-4 record against Pegula, wasn't at her best either, but she kept it together enough to cruise to a first set win.

Even baseline rallies, the area where Pegula is supposed to be one of the steadiest players on tour, weren't going her way, with a noticeably low ball-striking angle resulting in countless balls landing in the net.

Pegula was aware of her issues. She bounced her racket against the court in frustration at one point and ESPN cameras caught her telling her coaches that she has never double-faulted so many times in her life. Even her own coach Mark Knowles told ESPN she was playing too passively between sets.

"I wasn't exactly serving my best and I was fighting a lot of demons out there today," Pegula said in her post-match interview.

She got moderately better in the second set, but still had to dig deep to avoid a straight-sets loss. A late break allowed her to steal the set and stay alive.

Pegula's main adjustment appeared to be ramping down her serve velocity and trusting her baseline game. It worked, even if she still had to respond to a break by Navarro that put her down 2-1 in the third set. She did so by winning the next four games, cruising to a win that took a surprising amount of fortitude.

It's been a career season for Pegula, who leads the WTA in wins this year with 50, but what she would like most of all is a Grand Slam title. Every other player in the top 6, from Sabalenka to Noskova, has won one of the four trophies all players covet.

With her biggest success coming on hard court and friendly crowds at Flushing Meadows, the US Open has always loomed as her best shot at breaking through. She's two matches from accomplishing that, but the degree of difficulty is already looking like it will be very high.

images.caption: Jessica Pegula still has a path to the WTA's No. 1 ranking. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II)

articles.title: US Open: Frances Tiafoe consoles heartbroken Alex Michelsen after wild comeback
articles.summary: Frances Tiafoe pulled off the biggest comeback of the US Open. Then he helped produce one of the best moments of the US Open.
articles.body:
Frances Tiafoe pulled off the biggest comeback of the US Open. Then he helped produce one of the best moments of the US Open.

Following his thrilling, five-set comeback against Alex Michelsen , Tiafoe shared an embrace with his good friend and countryman after giving him the most painful loss of his career. Michelsen was clearly crying and left the court with a towel over his head.

Michelsen had the match in hand in the third set, holding a 7-5, 6-3, 5-3 lead at one point. He was serving for the set when he opened the game with back-to-back double-faults, giving Tiafoe all the runway he needed to get back in the match.

The 22-year-old Michelsen also was up a break in the fifth set but gave it back and eventually lost in a 10-point tiebreaker. It was the first Grand Slam quarterfinal of his career, and it ended as painfully as possible.

His embrace with Tiafoe quickly started going viral after the match, with Tiafoe sharing his perspective in an ESPN interview:

"As soon as I hugged him, I seen that he was crying already, I was like, 'Man I know. I've been there. I've been there twice, to be fair ... He's young, he hasn't been there. We're super-tight. We laugh and joke all the time, one of my good buddies on tour. I know how much that hurts. I know how much he wanted it today. It's something that you dream about. "I just told him, 'Bro, I know you're going to be here so many more times. I'm going to be in a rocking chair when you do so.'"

"As soon as I hugged him, I seen that he was crying already, I was like, 'Man I know. I've been there. I've been there twice, to be fair ... He's young, he hasn't been there. We're super-tight. We laugh and joke all the time, one of my good buddies on tour. I know how much that hurts. I know how much he wanted it today. It's something that you dream about.

"I just told him, 'Bro, I know you're going to be here so many more times. I'm going to be in a rocking chair when you do so.'"

Tiafoe is one of the most popular players on tour for a reason. In addition to being an exciting player who always seems to deliver in New York City, he is beloved among his peers. Michelsen certainly seemed to appreciate him while speaking with reporters after the match:

"I wasn't saying much, I was trying to keep it together and didn't do a good job of that. He was saying a lot of nice, personal things, 'You'll be there,' when I'm older. 'You're gonna be here. We're going to play again.' He's a great guy for consoling me in that moment."

Tiafoe will face another fellow American, No. 8 Ben Shelton, on Friday, after Shelton's late-night epic against Carlos Alcaraz .

images.caption: Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen are good friends off the court. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)

articles.title: Tennis: Meet the doubles team with a 66-year age gap
articles.summary: David McCandless, 80, and his 14-year-old doubles partner Liam teamed up two years ago – and they haven't looked back since.
articles.body:
They may be 66 years apart in age, but on the tennis court David McCandless and his doubles partner Liam have developed a partnership that has proved a winning combination.

The 80-year-old and his 14-year-old counterpart teamed up two years ago and have not looked back since.

Since then, the unlikely pairing have won more than half of their North West of Ireland league games - after ironing out a few kinks.

"We started on court and it was a case of who is going to go where," Liam said. "Then after a couple of matches we started winning because we realised we got a system down and we realised we are a pretty good duo."

David said the partnership came about "purely by accident" but two years later it had "worked out very well indeed".

"He's a very strong young junior and I think he will be a top class player," he said.

David was the same age as his partner when he first took up tennis and has loved every minute of his time on court, now playing up to four or five times a week.

He believes the experience he has gained over the years can complement Liam's coaching and natural ability.

"He got coaching from a young age which I never got," David said. "I wouldn't have the same ability in playing the correct shots. I'm just self-taught."

"I do have a bit of experience and I do think that I can help him as regards how to move on the court at times," he continued.

"And he knows what I'm capable of and he covers for me at other times."

Liam is equally complimentary about his older partner, saying he brings a lot of experience to the court.

"He's a solid player and consistent and I've learned a lot from him playing in the league," he said.

The pair are part of City of Derry Tennis Club, which now has about 100 members despite not having a clubhouse or courts of its own.

The club said its membership included people of all ages and backgrounds from across the community.

"That's something we pride ourselves on," club spokesman Keith Bloomfield said.

"We have a great cross community and cross border club and we have many foreign nationals now taking up the game - from India, Ukraine, and Malaysia amongst others."

And for those involved, tennis is about much more than winning matches.

Coach Catherine Gallen said the sport had become an important outlet for her.

"It's just so good for your physical and mental health," she said. "Like I'd come back from school and play tennis and it's just such a release.

"I've made so many friends from tennis. It's just so sociable."

"If you've had a tough day or you are going through something difficult just to get out there and hit those balls it's a fantastic release," she said.

But despite the club going from strength to strength, it faces a significant problem - it has no home of its own and has to rent different courts around Derry.

For decades, the tennis courts at St Columb's Park were regarded as the home of tennis in the city - and the club would like to see the site restored to its former glory.

"It is a great shame that such a beautiful and iconic facility cannot be restored," Bloomfield added. "What will happen to those courts?"

He said funding for repairing and upgrading the courts was not included in any council capital plans - and the club believes other towns have facilities that Derry is lacking.

"Neighbouring towns have bespoke clubs and clubhouses and facilities and it's a pity that a city the size of Derry doesn't have such a facility of its own," Bloomfield said.

Over the last two years, club representatives have met with council staff to discuss facilities for tennis in the city.

A spokesperson for Derry City and Strabane District Council said it recognised "the value of tennis and the very positive contribution local clubs make to the sport".

They said the council was aware of concerns regarding some facilities and representatives had met with the club to discuss ways to address them, and with Tennis Ireland and Sport NI to explore funding opportunities to upgrade existing courts.

"It is council's assessment that there is currently adequate provision for tennis across the city, based on existing capacity, usage levels and booking demands across available facilities," the spokesperson added.

The club said that, on paper, there were enough courts in the city - there are four at Waterside Shared Village, six at St Columb's Park and two at Clooney Park West, but the reality is a different story.

The St Columb's Park courts have been closed to the public throughout the summer pending a safety assessment, while the tarmac courts at Clooney Park are also said to be in poor condition.

That leaves the courts at Waterside Shared Village, where, the club said, even the line markings are showing their age.

For David and Liam, their unlikely partnership is a small example of what tennis can offer - regardless of age.

images.caption: David McCandless, 80, and his 14-year-old doubles partner Liam teamed up two years ago

articles.title: Tennis: Naomi Osaka makes passionate defence of on-court outfits at US Open
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka says any criticism she receives for her outfits is "worth it" if it means "the people after me have an easier path".
articles.body:
Naomi Osaka says any criticism she receives for her extravagant outfits is "worth it" if it means "the people after me have an easier path".

The 28-year-old is renowned for her eye-catching on-court attire, which included a hooded white gown for her first-round win against Anastasia Zakharova at the US Open.

Underneath was an all-black basketball-style kit in which Osaka played, while she also had her hair braided and wore a headband in a tribute to former NBA star Allen Iverson, who she called a "trailblazer" as "he's kind of like done a lot in fashion, whether it's on purpose or not".

In her latest outfit, Japan's four-time Grand Slam champion wore a decorated coat at the start of her last-16 US Open defeat by Elena Rybakina.

In defending her fashion statements, she referred to speaking out about her mental health in 2021 when she refused to speak to the media at the French Open and subsequently withdrew from the tournament.

Osaka, whose father is Haitian-American and mother is Japanese, also highlighted her ancestry.

"I don't mind being the first to do something and getting trashed for it," she wrote in a social media post.

"This happened when I talked about mental health and for some reason it's happening with my clothes lol.

"I'm literally Haitian it's in my blood to be this way, as long as the people after me have an easier path it's worth it."

articles.title: US Open: Ben Shelton powers through Carlos Alcaraz in historic, late-night thriller
articles.summary: Ben Shelton will face Frances Tiafoe in the semifinal, after the biggest win of his career.
articles.body:
The US Open men's final is guaranteed to feature a single American, courtesy of the biggest win, and latest night, of Ben Shelton's career.

In the final hour of Tuesday and the early hours of Wednesday, the No. 8 seed defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 in a Match of the Year candidate between two of the sport's young stars.

With the final shot landing at 3:33 a.m., the four-and-a-half-hour match featured the latest ending in US Open history, surpassing Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner's legendary clash in the 2022 quarterfinals (2:50 a.m.). The match ended so late that the cleaners started working inside Ashe in the fifth set .

Shelton's reward will be an All-American match against No. 11 seed Frances Tiafoe in the semifinal on Friday. Whoever wins will become only the second American man to reach the US Open in final in the past two decades (Taylor Fritz, 2024), looking to end a Grand Slam drought that goes back to Andy Roddick's US Open title in 2003.

Shelton did it against a seven-time Grand Slam champion who, to be fair, was also playing his first tournament in more than four months. Alcaraz had little trouble reaching the quarterfinals, dropping only one set in four matches, but Shelton always represented a different difficulty level, against whom Alcaraz would have to be fully functional.

Entering the match, Alcaraz was 14-0 in Grand Slams against Americans and 13-0 against left-handers. He had won 12 straight five-set matches and 18 overall. Shelton ended all of those streaks, picking up his first career Grand Slam win over a top-five player in the process.

Carlos Alcaraz-Ben Shelton lived up to the hype, for those who stayed up

From the moment the draw was revealed, this particular quarterfinal matchup was tantalizing for tennis fans. The pair are two of the hardest-hitting, quickest-moving, loudest-shouting, all-court players on tour. Entertainers, in addition to being elite tennis players at 23 years old.

It was the perfect showcase for modern tennis, so naturally the US Open's comically flawed schedule forced them to begin the proceedings around 11 p.m. local time. The first three matches at Arthur Ashe Stadium were all thrillers that went the distance, so fans at least got their money's worth.

Alcaraz-Shelton was worth staying up for. There was Shelton unleashing serves up to 150 mph and throwing down jumping volleys. There was Alcaraz reaching balls no other player is capable of touching. One such point:

The match began on even footing, with the pair staying on serve in the first set until it was 5-5, at which point they exchanged breaks to force a tiebreaker. Shelton led that at 5-3, only for Alcaraz to roar back with four straight points.

Alcaraz started the second set with a 14-point hold then similarly pushed Shelton's subsequent service game, but it was after that point something seemed to give.

There are plenty of possible explanations for why Alcaraz lost the next nine consecutive games. He could have felt something in his wrist and become more tentative. He could have tweaked something on an awkward jumping volley in that Shelton service game. He could have finally felt the exhaustion of playing his best opponent since losing to Jannik Sinner at Monte Carlo on April 12. He could have been saving energy for what was clearly to come.

Whatever happened, Alcaraz didn't move the way he usually does and committed an inordinate amount of unforced errors with a forehand that is usually among the best in tennis. He was a full step behind Shelton for a set and a half, only making things competitive in a third set where he couldn't get the necessary break to take back momentum.

It was a career-best effort by Shelton, who also showed a more reserved demeanor as the match went on and the possibility of an upset became more real. Shelton has always run hot and cold as a player, sometimes to his detriment, but his only reaction to his third-set win was a satisfied stare at his coach's box .

Alcaraz, of course, started feeling better, or at least started performing better. He got a break on his first opportunity in the fourth set and pressed that advantage into forcing the fifth set.

Along the way, he was seen heaving into his towel on a changeover . That was also around the time ESPN cameras caught new USTA president Craig Tiley appearing on the verge of falling asleep because, again, these guys were playing a match at an hour and length that would match a cross-country red-eye flight.

As the clock reached and then passed 3 a.m., the two men locked in for the most intense set of the match. Both faced break points in the fifth set, both saved them all. Shelton started emptying his emotional tank while Alcaraz looked increasingly at home, powered by the adrenaline that has made him nearly unbeatable in five-set matches.

It all came down to that final, 10-point tiebreaker. Shelton got it done, ending it all with a 146-mph ace.

articles.title: Alcaraz cede la corona de Nueva York en el súper 'tie break' ante Shelton
articles.standfirst: El duelo entre Ben y Tiafoe asegura la presencia de un estadounidense en la final del domingo
articles.summary: El duelo entre Ben y Tiafoe asegura la presencia de un estadounidense en la final del domingo
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz no se ha podido clasificar por cuarta vez en su carrera para las semifinales del Abierto de los Estados Unidos tras caer con el local Ben Shelton, por 5-7(5), 6-1, 6-3 y 7-6(7), en 4 horas y 28 minutos. Era apenas la segunda derrota de Alcaraz a cinco sets en 17 partidos, lo que enseña la dimensión del triunfo de Ben. El partido se inició a las 23.00 horas del martes en Nueva York después de las 2 horas y 20 minutos que se alargó el duelo de cuartos entre Jessica Pegula y Emma Navarro. Terminó a las 03.35 de la madrugada. La pista Arthur Ashe, la más grande del planeta tenis, se mantuvo llena para seguir el espectáculo ofrecido por Alcaraz y Shelton. "Ha sido un honor compartir la pista con Carlos", dijo el ganador a la conclusión. Ben estuvo en la pelea gracias a la inspiración con el servicio. Alcanzó puntas de 234 kilómetros por hora. Carlitos dio primero con un 'break' en el undécimo juego y sacó después para adelantarse en el marcador. Un par de derechas mal tocadas llevaron el desenlace a la muerte súbita. Alcaraz fue mejor a siete puntos y resoplaba porque el americano se había anotado el punto del torneo, en el 1-1. Shelton, que jugaba en casa, no iba a rendirse tan fácilmente y logró una doble segunda rotura para situar un tanteo favorable de 3-1 en la continuación. En el palco de Ben aplaudía su pareja, la estrella del fútbol americano Trinity Rodman. Con empate a una manga todo empezaba de cero. Era como jugar un partido del circuito ATP al mejor de tres sets. El cansancio, sin embargo, hacía más mella en el tenista con menos rodaje. Y ese era Alcaraz. Los 139 días sin competir se notaban, en especial en la puesta en escena de la pelota. Dos de los tres breaks concedidos en el segundo set habían sido con doble falta. Había decantado a su favor el 45 por ciento de los puntos con segundo saque. Ya eran ocho los juegos seguidos sumados por Shelton. Al pupilo de Samuel López también le penalizaba el 1/6 en pelotas de rotura. Atajó la sangría de juegos en contra con el 3-1. Lo que pasa es que el saque del americano no le dio opción para intentar remontar la tercera manga. Carlitos sufría desajustes en sus tiros propios del largo parón por la lesión en la muñeca derecha. El casillero de errores no forzados se disparaba hasta los 35. Alcaraz se agarró al cemento y buscó reengancharse al partido con una pelota de 5-4. El estadounidense la salvó a raquetazo limpio y suyo fue el tercer set. El murciano demostró toda su grandeza forzando el desempate cuando pocos le daban opción por su lenguaje corporal, con claros signos de cansancio. Shelton estaba ofuscado y no veía portería. Fue por ello que se marchó a los vestuarios para intentar cambiar el ritmo y la dinámica del partido. "Que te vea", le insistía Samuel a su pupilo. Los aficionados yanquis de la Arthur Ashe empezaron a gritar "USA, USA...". No era un partido de Copa Davis. El ruido en la central más grande del mundo llegaba a ser ensordecedor. A Ben se le escaparon tres pelotas de 5-3 porque su oponente le puso cabeza, corazón y cojones", el lema de su abuelo. "Let's go", soltaba el vigente campeón. Shelton se aseguró el súper 'tie break' y mandó toda la presión al otro lado de la red. Suyo fue finalmente el triunfo en el cara o cruz. Su servicio marcó la diferencia. La victoria del americano garantiza la presencia de un tenista local en la final del domingo. Y es que el verdugo de Alcaraz se cruzará este viernes con su compatriota Frances Tiafoe. El US Open se queda sin Carlitos y la grada sin sus celebtaciones.

images.caption: Alcaraz y Shelton se saludan en la red. BRIAN HIRSCHFELD
Carlitos logra devolver una pelota imposible.

articles.title: Ben Shelton beats Carlos Alcaraz in latest ever U.S. Open finish
articles.summary: There’s leaving it late, and then there’s what Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz just served up at the U.S.
articles.body: There’s leaving it late, and then there’s what Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz just served up at the U.S. Open. The American star ultimately outdueled the defending champion in the latest ever finish at the tournament, a thriller that didn’t finish until 3:33 a.m. in front of a raucous New York crowd. The five-set victory takes Shelton to the semifinals, where he will face fellow American Frances Tiafoe. That means there is guaranteed to be an American in Sunday’s final, hoping to end a drought that has seen no U.S. men’s player win a Grand Slam since Andy Roddick in New York in 2003. Shelton, the No. 8 seed, ended Alcaraz’ 18-match winning streak in Grand Slam tournaments in a clash that lasted 4 hours, 28 minutes. At one point, the Spaniard could be seen vomiting into a towel. The grueling quarterfinal was played under the lights after a day of marathon contests at Flushing Meadows. The highlight-filled match swung back and forth, with Shelton winning the second and third sets after losing the first on a tie break. No. 2 seed Alcaraz, who missed most of the season with a wrist injury, won the fourth set 6-1 to set up a grueling final set. The pair traded blows but ultimately couldn’t be separated until the final set tiebreaker, which Shelton won 10-7. The epic now stands as the latest finish in the history of a tournament increasingly known for its overnight duels. That honor had previously been held by another Alcaraz match, against his rival at the top of the sport Jannik Sinner, which finished at 2:50 a.m in the 2022 quarterfinals. That victory helped Alcaraz, then 19, on the way to his first U.S. Open title. He’ll now set his sights on regaining the form that made him the sport’s leading light. Three of Tuesday’s four singles quarterfinal matches went to match tiebreakers, the day starting with Aryna Sabalenka edging Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova to keep alive her hopes of a third straight U.S. title. Tiafoe then outlasted fellow American Alex Michelsen, staging repeated comebacks to set up the semifinal with Shelton. Thousands of fans stayed to the gripping end, with both Shelton and the popular showman Alcaraz enjoying loud support in Arthur Ashe Stadium. “It’s incredible,” Shelton said. “I always say that this is the greatest sports city in the world, I say that this is the greatest stadium in the world. I’m just hoping that my best friend and my sister over there don’t have to be at work at 6 a.m. in three hours.” Alcaraz said he could “leave the court happy,” and the seven-time Grand Slam champion offered praise for his American opponent. “I leave the court with a smile. I am proud of myself, how I fought,” he said. “Shelton played a very complete, very mature match,” Alcaraz added in Spanish. “He knew exactly what to do at every moment. And, physically, he’s a beast. It seemed like he had no weaknesses whatsoever.” Shelton summed up the evening. “It was a war,” he said. CORRECTION (Sept. 9, 2026, 8:25 a.m. ET): A headline and a previous version of this article misspelled the first name of an American tennis player. He is Frances Tiafoe, not Francis.

images.caption: Ben Shelton, of the United States, celebrates after a point Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, during the quarterfinal round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, in New York.
Alcaraz was playing his first tournament since April. Matthew Stockman / Getty Images

articles.title: Lo que le queda a Carlos Alcaraz: seis torneos seguros y uno más si España está en la final de la Copa Davis
articles.standfirst: El español regresa a España y no volverá a competir hasta el 25 de septiembre en la Laver Cup
articles.summary: El español regresa a España y no volverá a competir hasta el 25 de septiembre en la Laver Cup
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, tras caer eliminado en los cuartos del US Open a manos de Ben Shelton, terminando una racha de 18 victorias en los grandes, regresa a España. Descansará unos días antes de preparar su vuelta a la competición, que será en la Laver Cup 2026 (25 al 27). La novena edición del torneo ideado en su día por Roger Federer se celebrará en el O2 de Londres. Es la segunda vez que Europa y el Resto del Mundo se medirán en la capital británica. Hace cuatro años fue allí la retirada oficial de Federer en un histórico dobles con Rafael Nadal que acabaron perdiendo con los americanos Frances Tiafoe y Jack Sock. El pupilo de Samuel López, con un increíble tirón popular, se ha convertido en un fijo en la Laver Cup. Es su tercera presencia seguida. En 2024 lideró al equipo europeo a la victoria en Berlín. Alcaraz volará directamente de Londres a Tokio para defender la corona del torneo de categoría 500 (30 de septiembre al 6 de octubre). La gira asiática terminará para el campeón de siete grandes en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái (7 al 18 de octubre) del que se ausentó la pasada edición. En su regreso al viejo continente hará una parada en Riad para jugar por tercer año seguido el Six Kings Slam (21 al 24 de octubre). El murciano compartirá cartel con Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev, Novak Djokovic, Taylor Fritz y Alex de Miñaur. Como segundo en liza con más títulos de Grand Slam está exento de los cuartos y entrará directamente a jugar las semifinales del 22 de octubre. En Europa disputará el último Masters 1000 del curso en París (2 al 8 de noviembre) y las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22). En caso de que España se clasifique para la Final a 8 de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 al 29), estará en el equipo español buscando la séptima Ensaladera de la historia. El 12 de diciembre, en mitad de la pretemporada, el murciano tiene fijada una exhibición en Sao Paulo con el brasileño Joao Fonseca.

images.caption: Alcaraz ejecuta una volea.

articles.title: Los misiles de Shelton a 234 kilómetros por hora y el dormilón de Zverev
articles.standfirst: Alcaraz cogió fuerzas para enfrentarse a Shelton en un emblemático punto de Nueva York
articles.summary: Alcaraz cogió fuerzas para enfrentarse a Shelton en un emblemático punto de Nueva York
articles.body: Mientras Ben Shelton se ejercitaba el lunes en las pistas de Flushing Meadows, los aficionados buscaban a Carlos Alcaraz, un ídolo de masas en Nueva York y en cualquier punto del planeta al que viaja. El murciano decidió, junto a los miembros de su equipo, tomarse el día libre para ser un turista más en la ciudad de los rascacielos. Junto a su cuerpo técnico se desplazó al parque de Chelsea para estirar los músculos y conocer un enclave que destaca por la estatua Chelsea Doughboy: Dentro del propio parque, en el lateral de la Novena Avenida, se puede ver este histórico monumento de bronce de 1921 dedicado a los soldados locales de la Primera Guerra Mundial. Alcaraz también ha visitado el nuevo parque flotante. Alexander Zverev, primer cabeza de serie del cuadro individual masculino, ha jugado cuatro partidos y todos ellos han sido en el último turno de la sesión nocturna. Y lo mismo pasará este miércoles con el quinto, en los cuartos que le cruzarán ante Botic van de Zandschulp. Mientras la mayoría de jugadores prefieren evitar la sesión nocturna, para tener la tarde libre e irse antes a dormir. Zverev prioriza el sueño. En los Grand Slam, ha confesado que necesita entre 10 y 11 horas, y no le gusta madrugar. Solución: jugar de noche cuando nadie más quiere. Eso le permite librarse de las ruedas de prensa oficiales y se limita a dar un par de declaraciones en una especie de zona mixta. Wimbledon ha dicho basta a la corriente de poblar los torneos de 'influencers' con millones de seguidores en sus redes sociales, pero sin conocimiento de tenis. La ATP, en las finales de Turín 2025, fue la primera en abrir las puertas a los creadores de contenido invitando a 11 a la cita de maestros. Los 11 han pasado a 100 en el US Open. En Estados Unidos todo es a lo grande. Alcaraz no sólo destaca en la pista sino también con su banquillo. Al igual que el tenista, sus hombres de confianza tienen varias equipaciones estos días en Nueva York. En ella lucen cuatro de los patrocinadores del campeón de siete grandes: BMW, ElPozo, Isdin y Ant International. Este último va cambiando su denominación según la zona geográfica. Shelton ganó el partido de cuartos gracias a la poderosa arma que tiene en el servicio. En el segundo punto del partido fue capaz de mandar la pelota a 233 kilómetros por hora. De poco le sirvió tanta velocidad porque acabó por hincar la rodilla.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz’s US Open title defence ended in dramatic fashion as Ben Shelton defeated the defending champion in a thrilling five-set quarterfinal. The Spaniard fought back after losing the second and third sets, but could not complete the comeback. Shelton eventually won 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(7) in a match that finished after 2:50am in New York.Alcaraz also left fans concerned when he appeared to vomit into his towel after the fourth set. The 23-year-old had pushed himself through a gruelling contest against Shelton. The physical strain was clear as the match entered a deciding fifth set. Fans quickly reacted online to the extraordinary scenes before Shelton sealed a famous victory.Worried fans laud Carlos Alcaraz for his performance as he vomits before suffering heartbreaking US Open exitCarlos Alcaraz looked in control early in the match against Ben Shelton. He took the opening set 7-6(5) after a tense tiebreak. However, the American quickly changed the momentum.Shelton dominated the second set and won it 6-1. He then took the third set 6-3 to move within one set of a huge upset.Alcaraz refused to give up. The defending champion raised his level in the fourth set. He raced through it 6-1 and forced a deciding fifth set. But shortly after winning the set, Alcaraz appeared to be sick into his towel during the changeover.The moment immediately caught the attention of fans watching around the world.Alcaraz appeared to turn away from the court as he tried to recover. Former American tennis player James Blake said the Spaniard did not want the camera to show him being sick and asked the cameraman to look away. Despite the difficult moment, Alcaraz continued.Fans had already praised Alcaraz for continuing despite his physical struggles. One fan wrote, “The US Open conditions are brutal. Still fighting through it, that’s champion mentality.” Another wrote, “This is the part of Grand Slam tennis people sometimes forget. Your body can be screaming at you to STOP, the clock is ridiculous, you’re exhausted, and you still have to somehow find another level. Alcaraz is giving absolutely EVERYTHING out there.”Another fan simply reacted to the difficult sight involving the Spaniard, “noooo my bb”.Meanwhile, Shelton’s serving also earned plenty of praise. A user wrote, “Ben Shelton’s serve is UNMATCHED”As Alcaraz fought back in the fourth set, another fan celebrated his revival and wrote, “Carlos is looking alive!! VAAAAAMMMOOOOSSSS!”The game also produced plenty of excitement among neutral viewers. A fan wrote, “Alcaraz x Shelton was a treat for my eyes today”.Shelton held serve at the beginning of the fifth set, putting the Spaniard under immediate pressure. The fifth set eventually went to a deciding tiebreak.Shelton kept his composure and moved closer to one of the biggest wins of his career. He finally completed the upset by winning the tiebreak 10-7. His final blow was a 146mph serve out wide.The result sent Alcaraz out of the US Open and booked Shelton a place in the semi-finals against fellow American Frances Tiafoe.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Carlos Alcaraz beaten by Ben Shelton in epic quarter-final
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz's US Open title defence is over after a dramatic five-set quarter-final loss to Ben Shelton which ends at 03:34 local time.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz's US Open title defence came to an end in a dramatic five-set quarter-final loss to Ben Shelton which ended at 03:34 local time - the latest finish in the tournament's history.

A large crowd remained captivated deep into the night as a modern classic unfolded over an unpredictable four hours and 28 minutes on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

The match did not begin until about 11pm in New York, after the start of the night session was delayed by Tuesday's earlier matches.

At its conclusion, eighth seed Shelton basked in a standing ovation from a delirious audience after completing a 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7) victory that will live long in the memory of all those present.

"That was a war, an epic match, so physical," Shelton said.

"Carlos is one of the greatest champions in our sport already at 23 years old.

"It's ridiculous some of the stuff he comes up with sometimes - the most enjoyable match that I've had in my career, for sure."

This was the biggest - and certainly most significant - win of Shelton's career.

He had not beaten a top-three player in 17 attempts, and had lost each of his three previous matches against Spain's Alcaraz.

It also boosted home hopes of a first American men's singles champion in New York for 23 years.

Shelton was less than a year old when Andy Roddick won the US Open in 2003 - but an American finalist is guaranteed when he and Frances Tiafoe meet in Friday's semi-finals.

World number three Alcaraz was competing at his first tournament since a lengthy injury lay-off, but that is to take nothing away from Shelton, who produced a phenomenal performance.

Seven-time major winner Alcaraz had exceeded expectations on his return after more than four months out with a wrist injury, including sweeping past 20th seed Tommy Paul to reach the last eight.

But the 23-year-old's lack of match fitness appeared to finally catch up with him in a high-octane encounter filled with breathless exchanges and astounding displays of athleticism.

Even when it appeared Alcaraz had emptied the tank, the two-time winner not only forced a deciding set but would go the distance as the players engaged in a tense 10-point match tie-break that provided a fitting conclusion to the contest.

"It was close. So I'm just not going to be disappointed about not getting the win at the end," said Alcaraz.

"I'm just proud about myself, about how I fought. I leave the court with a smile, healthy, and this is what I needed."

While home hope Shelton had the vast support of the hardy crowd, Alcaraz has always felt at home at Flushing Meadows.

The Spaniard had won 28 of his 31 matches at the tournament - the highest win rate at the US Open in the sport's professional era at above 90% - and last year became the first man to reach the final without dropping a set since Roger Federer in 2015.

The Australian Open champion was also on an 18-match unbeaten streak at Grand Slam tournaments, having missed the French Open and Wimbledon with injury, and was seeking to reach his fourth New York semi-final in five years.

Regardless of his opponent's current levels, for Shelton this was a victory that could prove seismic in front of a home crowd who passionately backed him throughout.

"It is incredible, I always say that this is the greatest stadium in the world," the 23-year-old said.

"I'm just hoping my best friend and sister don't have to be at work at 6am. It would be huge from their employers to let them have the day off."

The American number one is through to his third major semi-final, having lost to two of the game's heavyweights in Jannik Sinner at last year's Australian Open and Novak Djokovic in New York three years ago. Both went on to be crowned champions.

After ousting Alcaraz, Shelton is now the second-highest ranked player remaining in the draw after world number two Alexander Zverev.

It remains to be seen how Shelton will recover for the semi-final against Tiafoe, who completed a remarkable comeback from two sets and a break down to beat compatriot Alex Michelsen.

"For me, it's always about the people in the crowd - whether it's my coaches and my team, all of my family and friends," Shelton said.

"The city of New York that showed up tonight until 3am, that's what kept me going."

Sabalenka fights back to keep US Open defence alive

Osaka makes passionate defence of on-court outfits

A closely contested first set offered a hint of the momentum swings that would define the match.

Alcaraz edged the opener on a tie-break - but only after surrendering his advantage after breaking for a seemingly decisive 6-5 lead.

Shelton, however, was ruthless as Alcaraz's level dropped sharply and embarked on a run of nine unanswered games to claim the second set and take charge of the third.

Refusing to fold, Alcaraz launched his fourth-set revival by saving two break points and then breaking when Shelton missed a backhand.

Alcaraz appeared to be sick into his towel during a changeover, such was his level of physical exertion, but would break Shelton a second time as he earned a fifth set as the time approached 02:30.

Both players failed to take break-point opportunities before a match-deciding breaker swung back and forth.

Shelton led 3-1 and Alcaraz regained control at 5-3.

But the Spaniard's uncharacteristically high number of unforced errors - the second seed made 53 overall - ultimately cost him, as Shelton captured five of the next six points before seeing out victory in style with an ace.

'An opponent has to take advantage - and Shelton did'

The first sign that all was not well with Alcaraz came at the end of the first set.

His forehand was off, and his serve erratic. Some of the rallies were stunning, but he was playing carelessly at times, and sometimes seemed disengaged as his concentration fluctuated.

All of which can be expected of someone who was playing just his fifth singles match since April and a first against a top-10 player.

But the opponent has to take advantage - and Shelton did so superbly.

Shelton has previously had a miserable record against the very best, losing all 17 of his previous matches against top-three players.

The flashy left-hander played plenty of shots and sent down one serve at 149mph, but was excellent on return and disciplined in defence.

By the fourth and fifth sets, Alcaraz was locked in again but could not prevent Shelton closing out the win of his life.

articles.summary: El murciano destaca la fortaleza física de Shelton al que define "como una bestia"
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha atendido a los cientos de medios desplazados a Nueva York nada más terminar el partido. Y lo ha hecho con una sonrisa en su rostro porque ha dejado atrás la lesión de la muñeca derecha que le tuvo parado 139 días. Por las altas horas de la madrugada se ha cambiado la sala de prensa por uno de los inmensos pasillos de la Arthur Ashe. "Me voy con la cabeza alta, contento y sano. He jugado contra una bestia. Tengo ganas de volver a casa y entrenar para lo que me queda. A veces se gana y a veces se pierde", reflexiona. El campeón de siete grandes reconoció que una de las claves del partido había estado en el servicio de su oponente: "Es que te mete mucha presión durante todo el tiempo. Ha habido momentos en los que podía haber hecho un poquito más. En el súper 'tie break iba dos puntos arriba y él ha sacado un segundo y yo he fallado el resto. Quién sabe si se hubiera jugado habría cambiado el partido ". Fue precisamente un saque directo del estadounidense el que cerró el triunfo. "La pelota por la noche se pone muy grande por la humedad y es difícil de manejar. Hace que el partido sea aún más duro. Delante tenía a un Shelton que ha jugado un partido muy completo, muy maduro y sabiendo en todo momento lo que tenía que hacer. Físicamente es una bestia, parecía que no tenía ningún tipo de debilidad", dice el número tres mundial. "Después del tercer set, he encontrado la manera de volver al partido. Me he apoyado en la gente, me animé y me vine arriba, y creo que lo conseguí hasta el último punto", continúa.

articles.title: US Open: Ben Shelton beats Carlos Alcaraz in five-set thriller in latest-ever finish to US Open match at 3.33am
articles.summary: Ben Shelton clinches first-ever victory over top-three opponent as he beats Carlos Alcaraz to set up US Open semi-final showdown with Frances Tiafoe; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
The American prevailed 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7) over four hours and 28 minutes to reward a raucous Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd gripped until 3.33am in what was the latest-ever finish to a US Open match.

It marked Shelton's first career win over a top-three player, against which he had been 0-17 coming into the match.

Shelton will now play Frances Tiafoe in the final four after his fellow countryman's thrilling five-set victory over Alex Michelsen earlier in the evening.

"For me it's always about the people in the crowd, whether it's my coaches, team or friends and family, or the city of New York that showed up tonight until 3am with the USA chants, that's what kept me going and what got me this win," Shelton said on-court.

"It's incredible. This is the greatest sports city and greatest stadium in the world. I'm hoping my best friend and sister don't have to be at work at 6am.

"I'm so grateful, so blessed to be in front of you guys and share the court with Carlos is an absolute honour."

Shelton's victory means the United States is guaranteed representation in Sunday's men's final, with Andy Roddick the last American man to win a major title back in 2003.

It also spelled the end of Alcaraz's courageous return to the court having been out for more than four months with a wrist injury and initially been a doubt to compete in New York.

The seven-time major champion, playing his first tournament since April, was seen vomiting before the beginning of the final set, which culminated in a 10-point match-deciding tie-break.

"As I said before the tournament began, the expectation was to go there, compete... playing these kind of matches, for me being healthy," said Alcaraz. "It was close, it really was close. So I'm just a little bit disappointed, about, (not) getting the win at the end.

"But, I'm just happy, I'm just proud about myself, about how I fought. After the third set, physically I was really tired, but I found a way to push myself up, physically give an extra. In the fifth set

"I just started to feel better and better. I was playing against one of the... he is a beast. He's an unbelievable player. Powerful. He just managed how to play really, really well in every situation, so credit to him. I leave the court happy, I leave the court with a smile, healthy, and this is what I needed."

Shelton heads into his third Grand Slam semi-final having previously reached the final four of the 2023 US Open and the 2025 Australian Open.

Having lost the opening tie-break, the 23-year-old stormed to nine straight games on his way to dominant second and third sets. Back came Alcaraz to send it to a decider, where he would win four successive points to lead 5-3 in the tie-break before inviting Shelton to turn things around.

In true Shelton fashion, he iced the game with a serve of 146mph that Alcaraz failed to tame, bringing the New York crowd to their feet.

"I remember, the last tiebreak that I played was in Paris," recalled Alcaraz. "It was an unbelievable game that I played in that moment. This time, when you are trying to fight and trying to overcome all the problems you might have - physically, tired a lot, obviously when he's serving, he puts a lot of pressure on you.

"You're thinking about, trying to put the return in, and it's unknown if you're going to play the point or he's going to get a free point with the serve. I think in these moments he takes a lot of advantage with serve, but not any excuse, but I would say it's an important weapon in these moments."

Tiafoe reaches US Open semis in thrilling fightback

Frances Tiafoe recovered from two sets down and ‌erased a 0-3 deficit in the fifth set to beat American compatriot Alex Michelsen 5-7 3-6 7-5 6-3 7-6 (10-6), reaching the semi-finals for a third time.

The 11th seed ​appeared to have lost all the magic of his early campaign before claiming the momentum in the third set and clinching ​it with a forehand winner to the deafening cheers of ‌the fans on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Michelsen had flown under the radar in his deepest major run but ​earned respect on the biggest stage of American tennis with 21 aces, and Tiafoe cut his own celebration short to comfort the 22-year-old in an emotional ​embrace.

"I hope he gets tight," Tiafoe said of his mindset at 4-5 down in the third set. "He gave me some gifts, a couple of double faults there.

"But then I slowly started to get my rhythm there, snuck out the third set and slowly started playing better and better.

"He is a hell of a player. He should've easily won today, so shout out Alex Michelsen."

Tiafoe joined Andre Agassi as the only American men to reach three US Open semi-finals in this century and will return to the top 10 for the first time in three years in the rankings.

"Everyone was sleeping in the first couple of hours and I was asleep with you all," Tiafoe joked following his win.

"As it went along, the energy was incredible, as always. Thank you [to the crowd] for being there for me. I really appreciate that."

"You can't help but feel sorry for Alex Michelsen considering how close he was and we all know Frances is a fan favourite in this situation.

"The tears started coming from Michelsen. It was like a punch in the gut for me and I don't even know him.

"Having been in these situations when you're so close to the finishing line and you know it's on your racket, I think that's the worst feeling. You know that you kind of did choke a little bit. That's the absolute worst.

"Brutal day for him but you have to tip your cap to Frances for turning that match around."

The US Open is live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App . You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: American Ben Shelton beats Carlos Alcaraz in latest-ever US Open finish
articles.summary: US tennis star Ben Shelton eventually got the better of Carlos Alcaraz in the latest-ever finish in US Open history, ending the Spaniard’s title defense and progressing to an all-American semifinal.
articles.body: US tennis star Ben Shelton eventually got the better of Carlos Alcaraz in the latest-ever finish in US Open history, ending the Spaniard’s title defense and progressing to an all-American semifinal. The titanic quarterfinal lasted four hours and 28 minutes, eventually ending at 3:33 a.m. local time in New York’s Arthur Ashe Stadium. The match was as dramatic as it sounds, with momentum swinging between the two players battling it out on court. It all appeared to be going to plan for Alcaraz after he won the first-set tiebreak, but Shelton stormed back in the next two sets to take a 2-1 lead in the match. But the Spaniard won the fourth set to take the contest to a deciding set that went the distance. With thousands of fans sticking around to watch the epic, Shelton was buoyed by the home support and found the energy to edge the match-deciding tiebreak and win the record-breaking quarterfinal in five sets – 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(7). “I mean, it’s incredible,” Shelton said after securing the win with a monster 146-mph serve. “I always say this is the greatest sports city in the world, the greatest stadium in the world.” He added: “For me, it’s always about the people in the crowd. Whether it’s my coaches and my team over there or my family and friends over here. “Or the city of New York that showed up tonight until 3 a.m., with the ‘U-S-A’ chants until the very end. That’s what kept me going, and that’s what got me this win tonight.” It was a brilliant performance from Shelton, who beat a top-3 player for the first time in his career. He made just 35 unforced errors and hit 34 winners to reach the third grand slam semifinal of his career. He will now face compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the semifinal, meaning an American will be in the final of the men’s US Open this year. Not since Andy Roddick in 2003 has an American man won a major title. This might be the country’s best chance for quite some time, given that the likes of Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic and Jannik Sinner are not in the picture. For Alcaraz, the loss brings an end to his title defense this year after a difficult season plagued by injury. The Spaniard missed both Wimbledon and the French Open but did win the Australian Open title at the start of 2026 – his seventh major trophy. The world No. 3 was typically gracious in defeat, smiling and waving to the crowd as he walked off the court, acknowledging the fans who had stayed until the bitter end. “It was close. I’m just a bit disappointed by not getting the win at the end,” he told reporters. “I’m just happy, I’m just proud of myself. After the first set, physically I was really tired, but I found a way to push myself up and physically give extra. In the fifth, I just started to feel better and better. “But you know, I was playing against someone that is a beast. You know, Shelton is an unbelievable player, powerful. He just manages to play really, really well in every situation. So credit to him. “But you know, I just leave the court happy. I leave the court with a smile, healthy, and this is what I need.”

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz Loses to Ben Shelton, Updated US Open Men's Tennis Bracket After Tuesday Results
articles.summary: Reigning U.S. Open champion Carlos Alcaraz was upset 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (7), in the quarterfinals of the 2026 U.S. Open at Arthur Ashe Stadium in Queens, New York, on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Reigning U.S. Open champion Carlos Alcaraz was upset 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (7), in the quarterfinals of the 2026 U.S. Open at Arthur Ashe Stadium in Queens, New York, on Tuesday night.

Following a late start, the match poured over into the wee hours of Wednesday morning, and it came to an end about four-and-a-half hours after it started, concluding at 3:33 a.m. ET, per ESPN .

For the eighth-seeded Shelton, it was arguably the biggest win of his career, as he took down the No. 2 seed and No. 3 player in the world to reach his third Grand Slam semifinal.

A career Grand Slam winner, the 23-year-old Alcaraz made his long-awaited return at the U.S. Open after missing both the French Open and Wimbledon with a wrist injury.

Despite the long layoff, he was considered the odds-on favorite, especially with world No. 1 Jannik Sinner not playing in the tournament due to a knee ailment.

Alcaraz ran into the hard-serving Shelton in the quarters, though, and he did so on Shelton's home soil.

Seemingly feeding off the atmosphere, Shelton was the better player on Tuesday night, breaking Alcaraz's serve five times compared to the three breaks Alcaraz got on him.

On top of that, Shelton committed only 35 unforced errors over the course of the five-set match, whereas Alcaraz made an uncharacteristic 53 unforced errors.

With No. 11 Frances Tiafoe beating fellow American Alex Michelsen earlier Tuesday, it means an American player is guaranteed to play in the U.S. Open men's singles final.

Either Shelton or Tiafoe will become the first American man to reach a Grand Slam singles final since Taylor Fritz at the 2024 U.S. Open. Before that, Andy Roddick was the last American man to make it to a Grand Slam singles final at Wimbledon 2009.

Roddick is also the most recent American men's Grand Slam singles champion, winning the U.S. Open back in 2003.

After squeaking past Alcaraz, Shelton is favored to take down Tiafoe and reach his first Grand Slam singles final where he would meet one of top-seeded Alexander Zverev, No. 28 Alexander Blockx, Botic van de Zandschulp or Karen Khachanov.

Following his marathon victory over Alcaraz, Shelton is scheduled to be back in action Friday when he and Tiafoe determine which American will go on to play for the U.S. Open title.

articles.title: Ben Shelton takes down Carlos Alcaraz to earn the biggest win of his career in latest US Open match ever
articles.summary: Ben Shelton defeated Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set thriller at Arthur Ashe Stadium, snapping the Spaniard's 18-match Grand Slam winning streak.
articles.body: It may have happened during a quarter-final match, and it may have taken place while most of the country was asleep, but Ben Shelton officially became the face of American men's tennis on Wednesday morning at the US Open. After four hours and 28 minutes of war, Shelton secured his victory over seven-time major champion Carlos Alcaraz 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-7) at 3:33 a.m. in New York, making it the longest match in the Grand Slam's history when the clock ticked past 2:50 a.m. By punching his ticket into the US Open semifinal for the second consecutive year, he guaranteed that the United States will be represented in Sunday's final as he'll take on fellow American Francis Tiafoe on Friday in the semis. GROUP OF INFLUENCERS FORCES PAUSE DURING US OPEN MATCH WITH CRINGEWORTHY PHOTOSHOOT IN SUITE An American man has not won a Grand Slam title since Andy Roddick took down Juan Carlos Ferrero at the 2003 US Open. Shelton certainly had the crowd on his side throughout the match, and admitted that he fed off of the American fans in New York. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "It’s always about the people in the crowd, whether it’s my coaches and my team over there, all my family and friends over here, or the city of New York," Shelton said during his on-court interview following the match. "They showed up tonight till 3 a.m. with USA chats until the very end, that’s what kept me going, and that’s what got me this win tonight. "I’m just hoping my best friend and my sister over there don’t have to be at work at 6 a.m. in three hours." LADIES AT THE US OPEN WERE CAUGHT ON CAMERA TAKING NOTICE OF A SHIRTLESS CARLOS ALCARAZ Shelton's heroics on Arthur Ashe Stadium on Tuesday night and into Wednesday morning snapped Alcaraz's 18-match winning streak in Grand Slam tournaments. As expected, Alcaraz made life tough for Shelton at pivotal points throughout the match, but the Spaniard's 53 unforced errors proved to be a critical difference in the end. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Shelton's serve, the strongest weapon in his repertoire, was on full display as he secured seven aces and just two double faults throughout the five-set thriller. The victory marked Shelton's first time defeating Alcaraz in his career, with the Spaniard previously holding a 3-0 record against the Florida native, with the two last meeting at Roland Garros in 2025.

articles.title: 2026 US Open TV schedule, quarterfinal matches on today – September 9
articles.summary: American tennis star Coco Gauff is among the athletes taking the court in Wednesday's quarterfinal action at the 2026 US Open.
articles.body:
The 2026 US Open quarterfinals continue on Wednesday, September 9, following an epic day full of deciders on Tuesday. The action at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center continued into the wee hours of the morning, with American tennis star Ben Shelton outdualing defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a thrilling five-setter that ran until 3:30 a.m. ET.

Luckily, fans should not run into the same issues on Wednesday night, with the final match of the day currently scheduled to begin at 7:30 p.m. ET when No. 1 men's seed Alexander Zverev faces off against Botic van de Zandschulp of the Netherlands.

All four of Wednesday's quarterfinal matches, which includes Coco Gauff vs. Mirra Andreeva, will take place on the Arthur Ashe Stadium court.

The action gets underway at 11:30 a.m. ET when surging Chinese star Qinwen Zheng looks to keep her impressive run in Queens going when she faces No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina.

Tennis – U.S. Open – Flushing Meadows, New York, United States – September 7, 2026 China's Qinwen Zheng in action during her round of 16 match against Poland's Iga Swiatek REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz Credit: REUTERS (Reuters)

Leading into the nightcap, Karen Khachanov faces No. 28 seed Alexander Blockx.

When and where can you tune into Wednesday's quarterfinal action throughout the day?

A full look at the US Open TV schedule for September 9 can be seen below.

2026 US Open TV Schedule – Wednesday, September 9

Mirra Andreeva (5) vs. Coco Gauff (4), 12:40 p.m. ET | Arthur Ashe Stadium | ESPN, Fubo ( try for free )

Karen Khachanov vs. Alexander Blockx (28), 2:00 p.m. ET | Arthur Ashe Stadium | ESPN, Fubo ( try for free )

Alexander Zverev (1) vs. Botic van de Zandschulp, 7:30 p.m. ET | Arthur Ashe Stadium | ESPN, Fubo ( try for free )

The 2026 US Open will wrap up this coming weekend with the women's singles final set for Saturday, September 12, and the men's singles final on Sunday, September 13, at Arthur Ashe Stadium. Official times for the championship matches have not been set.
